summary: PASS — Discover Shop-for caching bug fix VERIFIED end-to-end in the visible UI (no app reload). The frontend fix is confirmed effective: (a) discover.tsx query key now includes profile.preferences.shop_for and (b) profile.tsx save onSuccess invalidates ['catalogue-recommendations']. Executed the exact Women→Men→Women→Men sequence in a single app session at 390x844 against https://style-scan-v3.preview.emergentagent.com with brand-mention counts asserted against the rendered Discover DOM AND the backend /api/profile.preferences.shop_for after each save. Results: [1:Women] backend=womens, Figl=8 mentions, men brands (Henderson/Pierre Cardin/Anais/Obsessive)=0 — PASS. [2:Men] backend=mens, Figl=0, men brand mentions = {Henderson:12, Pierre Cardin:2, Anais:4, Obsessive:2} — PASS. [3:Women] backend=womens, Figl=8, men brands=0 — PASS. [4:Men] backend=mens, Figl=0, men brands total=20 — PASS. ZERO cross-department leakage after each switch. Also re-ran the full live backend regression suite (backend/tests/test_shop_for_e2e.py) — 11/11 passed in 12s: mens-only, womens-only, all-mode, pricing (113679==11.13, 111506==16.13), no metadata leak (department/provider_id/provider_kind/source_url/availability absent), full product field payload with non-empty recommendation_reasons, budget filter still applies (budget_max=15 under shop_for=all keeps every item ≤15), prepare-tryon(113679) no 'matterhorn'/no preview_url, colour conflict → 400, and ONE men's tryon generation (listed by /api/tryons). Profile was reset to shop_for='all' at the end of the UI run (verified by GET /api/profile).

issues: Harness-level only (not a product bug): the floating bottom tab bar occasionally lets a Discover product image intercept clicks on the Save button and tab labels. Mitigation used: scroll ScrollView to top before tapping a tab, scroll the Save button into view before clicking with retries + JS click fallback. Consider adding testID='tab-you' / testID='tab-discover' / testID='tab-stylist' / testID='tab-tryon' on the Tabs.Screen so future UI tests can click tabs directly without relying on visible text.

critical_code_review_comments: discover.tsx L24: query key is now ['catalogue-recommendations', profile?.preferences?.shop_for, profile?.updated_at] — any shop_for change forces a brand-new query and remount of the result, so stale men's/women's cards cannot linger across a department switch.

profile.tsx L91-97: save.onSuccess invalidates BOTH ['profile'] and ['catalogue-recommendations']. This belt-and-braces approach guarantees Discover refetches even if Discover is already mounted (the previous bug: Discover was never invalidated when Shop-for changed).
Backend hard department filter (product_recommendations.rank_verified_products) applies BEFORE scoring — unit + E2E suites green; no leakage path.
customer_recommendations payload remains allow-list projected — department/provider_id/provider_kind/source_url/availability absent across every item under all three shop_for modes.
No new deprecated expo packages detected on files-of-reference; no SafeAreaView regressions; no raw text outside <Text>.

rca_of_issue: Root cause confirmed: Discover's useQuery key was ['catalogue-recommendations', profile?.updated_at] — it was not keyed on preferences.shop_for AND profile.tsx's save.onSuccess invalidated only ['profile'], never ['catalogue-recommendations']. When profile.updated_at did refresh after a save, the cached (previous department's) recommendations stayed in RAM because React Query treats same-key cached data as fresh for the configured staleTime, and the Discover screen rendered the stale list → user perceived a 'mixture'. Fix applied by main agent: (1) include profile?.preferences?.shop_for in the Discover query key so any department switch produces a different cache entry and forces a refetch, (2) invalidate ['catalogue-recommendations'] inside profile.tsx save.onSuccess as belt-and-braces. Verified in this iteration: four consecutive in-UI switches without reload show the correct department-only brands at each step (Women→Men→Women→Men) with ZERO cross-department leakage, and the backend profile.preferences.shop_for value echoes the chip chosen.
